races.name: Sky Bet Mile Handicap Stakes (Heritage Handicap)

runners_data.name: Exclusive Code
runners_data.note: Won twice over this trip on good ground but has zero wins or places in soft/similar going (1 run, unplaced); James Doyle is a smart pilot for big-field handicaps but the going query is real and her prominent style may leave her exposed in a hot pace.
runners_data.comment: Exclusive Code bounced back to win last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making him a genuine threat at 135 lb from stall 11; the main concern is a trainer without a winner in twenty-five attempts over the last fortnight.

runners_data.name: St Anton
runners_data.note: Three wins from four starts over a mile on good, but only 1 place from 8 runs in similar going — the soft is a genuine concern for this front-of-the-pack type who needs to dominate; Richard Hannon's 3/53 recent strike rate is unremarkable but the horse's form profile is solid on quick ground.
runners_data.comment: Three wins in his last five starts, including a victory last time out and again three starts back, mark St Anton as a serious contender; the 41-day absence is the one factor to weigh against him.

runners_data.name: Outback Heat
runners_data.note: One of the confirmed pace-setters who is almost certain to be on the front end from the off; Kaiya Fraser is a claiming jockey which matters in a competitive heritage handicap, and 64 days off the track adds a fitness question mark, though Harry Eustace's recent 4/14 record suggests the yard is in form.
runners_data.comment: Outback Heat arrives on the back of a win two starts back and a second last time out, showing consistent form across his last four starts; he has experience over today's trip and our rating has him top-rated, albeit with company, with 64 days between runs the only minor query.

runners_data.name: Command The Stars
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse who drops back to a mile having run over longer trips, with his best recent run a third over 8f on good; the 7s in recent form are a concern, but he has shown form in similar conditions and Darragh Keenan gives him a shot from off the pace if the race pans out as expected.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Command The Stars does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and 25 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh; however, a disqualification on latest outing and a string of sevenths before that leave plenty to prove off 130 lb.

runners_data.name: Blue Courvoisier
runners_data.note: A confirmed front-runner who won over course and distance, making him one of the most likely horses to actually secure a lead position; Clive Cox's yard is in strong form (6/22) and Rossa Ryan is well-equipped for big-field navigation, though three rivals may test his ability to dictate.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out gives Blue Courvoisier a recent form boost, and his trainer is firing at 27% over the past fortnight, but an unplaced run two starts back and a speed rating of 87 suggest he remains one to treat cautiously from stall 5 at 128 lb.

runners_data.name: Noelan Star
runners_data.note: Consistent type who won over course and distance on fast ground and has winning form on AW; Daniel Tudhope is outstanding around York and Edward Bethell's yard is firing (9/25), making this a yard-jockey combination to respect in a heritage handicap with a pace that should suit a cover-and-pounce approach.
runners_data.comment: Noelan Star won last time out and has experience over today's trip, with his trainer firing at 36% in the past fortnight — strong positives; however, he carries 128 lb from stall seven and an unplaced run two starts back tempers enthusiasm slightly.

runners_data.name: Zennor Storm
runners_data.note: Won over this trip on AW and ran second over course and distance last time; Tom Marquand rides for Haggas who is in excellent recent form (7/38), and headgear worn (p) suggests he needs covering up — the expected strong pace suits that approach perfectly if he can avoid traffic.
runners_data.comment: Caught the eye when runner-up last time out and a winner five starts back, though two unplaced efforts in between temper enthusiasm; has run over today's trip and returns on a workable 22-day break carrying 128 lb from stall four.

runners_data.name: Lion of Alba
runners_data.note: A confirmed front-runner who has been beaten in seven of his last eight starts, including in soft and similar conditions; the tongue-tie is noted, but the recent form figures of 7-7-4-7 suggest he will lead for a time before weakening — David Probert will need to judge the gallop carefully.
runners_data.comment: Lion of Alba brings distance and going experience to this, and our rating of 100 ranks him second among 20 rivals, suggesting he holds strong claims on his best form — that win in his last five starts shows the ability is there, but a struggling trainer at 1/28 over the past fortnight is the concern.

runners_data.name: Welbury
runners_data.note: Six-timer in his last six, including back-to-back wins over this course and trip, and Edward Bethell's stable is red-hot; Oisin Orr has ridden him to victory before and his hold-up style is textbook for this pace scenario on soft ground — the headgear worn (p) and only 13 days between runs are the only mild queries.
runners_data.comment: Welbury won last time out and scored two starts back as well, so he arrives on the back of back-to-back victories and in sound nick at just 13 days since last seen; he has run over today's trip before, and a trainer firing at 36% strengthens the case, though stall 19 and a speed figure of 77 suggest he may need things to fall right from out wide.

runners_data.name: Intense Vision
runners_data.note: Flagged as fading in the finish, which is a serious concern in a soft-ground stamina test; the form figures of 3-0-0 in recent starts and a trainer who is 0/2 in the past 14 days make this an easy horse to put offside, regardless of his winning form earlier in the season.
runners_data.comment: Intense Vision has shown he can win at this level, scoring back-to-back victories four and five starts back, though two unplaced efforts in his last two runs give pause; he has run over today's trip before and returns after a 22-day break carrying 126 lb from stall 16.

runners_data.name: Jeddaal
runners_data.note: Won over this distance in soft going and has placed at similar; Kieran Shoemark rides well in big fields and Ed Walker's yard is ticking over (4/42), making this a solid each-way profile from a prominent position if the pace causes chaos ahead of him.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well down the field on our figures, Jeddaal faces a stiff ask from stall 12 carrying 125 lb, and a fourth last time out does little to inspire confidence, though he has shown he can win at this level, with two victories in his last five starts and experience of today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Ironwill
runners_data.note: Improving type who has placed twice in recent starts after winning over 7f; now stepping up to a mile for the first time and that trip question needs answering — Marco Ghiani rides confidently and the prominent style keeps him in touch, but the distance is a genuine unknown on a soft surface.
runners_data.comment: Placed second last time out and a winner two starts back, Ironwill brings fair recent form to the table, and has run over today's trip before; however, he faces 19 rivals and his 124 lb burden from stall 17 may test his resolution.

runners_data.name: Bearish
runners_data.note: Won twice this season, including over this course and trip on good ground, and is a hold-up horse for Oisin Murphy — one of the finest riders at getting horses into position in big-field handicaps; 47 days since last run and no soft-ground form are mild flags, but the profile suits the expected race shape well.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well adrift of the field on our figures, Bearish is hard to fancy at these weights despite a winner last time out and a second two starts back, and 47 days off adds a fitness query, though he has run over today's trip and draws stall two.

runners_data.name: Eklleem
runners_data.note: A confirmed pace type ridden by William Buick who won over this trip; 64 days off the track and no realistic winning form in soft or similar going (0W 0P from 1 sim-going run) mean Buick's class in the saddle may not be enough to overcome the conditions concern.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 19 of 20 on our figures, Eklleem faces a stiff ask under 123 lb from stall 15, and 64 days off adds a fitness query — yet he did win last time out and has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Krasimir
runners_data.note: Consistent without winning, placing three times in his last four over this distance; Colin Keane is a top-class operator, the trainer G M Lyons sends runners over from Ireland suggesting confidence, and tongue-tie plus headgear worn suggest a horse that needs specific conditions — the soft is unproven.
runners_data.comment: Placed in all five of his last starts with a win two starts back, Krasimir brings distance and going experience to the table, though third last time out tempers expectations slightly; 122 lb from stall ten gives him every chance at a mark of 86.

runners_data.name: Astrazar
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's horse won over 7f and placed over this trip; in truth a prominent racer whose natural racing position cannot be secured in this field given the volume of pace — Ashley Lewis takes a 3lb claim and the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.94 reflects that racing out of role will temper his chance significantly.
runners_data.comment: Placed second last time out after a couple of disappointing efforts, Astrazar showed he retains ability, and he has run over today's trip before; however, carrying 121 lb from stall 20 and a speed rating of 80 give the opposition something to work with.

runners_data.name: Storming Point
runners_data.note: Placed five times in six recent starts and clearly consistent, but his natural prominent style is one of several competing for a position the field cannot deliver for all of them — Rob Hornby is an experienced rider but soft ground and the likely back-of-the-group position in practice reduce his winning chance materially.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 18th of 20 on our figures, Storming Point has experience of today's distance and going but that sixth last time out does little to inspire confidence, despite his consistency at placed level in the runs prior.

runners_data.name: Daydreama
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for James Sullivan and Tim Easterby, whose yard sends out a high volume of runners (5/84 recent strike rate reflects that context); form has been workmanlike at best in this company and on good ground, with soft ground offering some unexplored upside but no confirmed benefit.
runners_data.comment: Daydreama was runner-up last time out and showed similar form a second six starts back, yet has been largely out of the money in between, leaving him winless in his last six starts; experience over today's trip and going helps his cause, though a mark of 84 and our rating of 96 suggest he carries weight to overcome from stall 8.

runners_data.name: Start Me Up
runners_data.note: Won on soft ground over 6f and has winning form, but stepping up sharply in trip and class here; the headgear (tp) and amateur-level soft-ground form at shorter trips make this a speculative profile — Saffie Osborne is a capable rider but the trip and OR jump are real hurdles.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well down our assessments among a field of twenty, Start Me Up is hard to fancy on his two most recent efforts — sixth and fourth — even if two wins in his last six starts show he retains ability; has run over today's trip and returns on a workable 20-day break.

runners_data.name: Le Samourai
runners_data.note: A confirmed front-runner from Ralph Beckett's well-respected yard, placed over this trip last time; tongue-tie is worn, soft ground has produced a poor run previously (10th), and Edward Greatrex takes over the ride — the going concern and the number of rivals intent on leading make his position hard to secure cleanly.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and with a speed rating that makes the task look stiff, Le Samourai is hard to fancy at face value despite a yard operating at a 28% strike rate; second last time out is a plus, and he has run over today's trip before, but the weight of the ratings evidence is against him.

races.paceDynamic: Outback Heat, Blue Courvoisier, Lion of Alba, and Le Samourai all want the lead in a 20-runner soft-ground mile at York, guaranteeing a strong, relentless gallop from the off with no prospect of a false pace — the field will be strung out early and stamina will be the defining quality. With eight horses competing for prominent positions, there will be fierce jostling for the first couple of furlongs and serious traffic danger two to three furlongs out as the field concertinas into the straight. This pace shape overwhelmingly favours genuine hold-up horses and horses with high cruising efficiency who can be produced late from midfield, as the strong early fractions will soften those who burn energy disputing the pace. The field contains more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate — Storming Point and Astrazar are natural prominent racers who are likely to be shuffled further back than ideal, with Outback Heat and Blue Courvoisier best placed to actually secure the pace positions they want.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the confirmed front runners set a genuine end-to-end gallop on soft ground and the field comes home on fumes.
scenarios.body: Outback Heat and Blue Courvoisier burn through the first half mile at a punishing clip, leaving the prominent horses legless turning in and gifting a clear run to horses produced from behind the pace; soft ground amplifies the stamina test and rewards those who travel within themselves deepest into the race. Hold-up horses like Welbury and Command The Stars, plus well-positioned midfielders like Bearish, are ideally placed to pick up the pieces in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runners Die, Mid-Pack Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses the leaders and a well-covered prominent horse arrives on the bridle at the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Noelan Star or Zennor Storm, sitting just off the pace under a confident hold, avoid the worst of the early scrimmaging and find daylight entering the straight as the leaders weaken; their ability to race prominently without actually leading means they conserve enough energy to sustain a run through soft ground to the line. This shape rewards horses who ran top-two-year-old form over this course and distance and whose trainer-jockey partnerships (Haggas/Marquand, Bethell/Tudhope) are dialled in at this meeting.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Leaders Outstay Rivals
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves even rather than frantic and one of the front runners finds the soft ground suiting their stamina rather than killing their speed.
scenarios.body: Blue Courvoisier, who won over this course and distance, or Le Samourai, stepping up in trip on going that suits, could find that the field chasing them runs out of momentum before they do; with 20 runners creating traffic for the closers, a horse slipping the field from the front at the two-furlong marker can find enough daylight to hold on. This scenario is most plausible if the early pace is slightly less extreme than billed and one front-runner conserves enough to last home.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos, Lucky Escapee
scenarios.trigger: If severe mid-race congestion between the two- and three-furlong markers blocks the closers and a horse that threads a gap from an unexpected position wins.
scenarios.body: With 20 runners on a soft surface, the straight will be chaotic and a horse like Ironwill or Krasimir — sitting close enough to avoid the worst of the bunching but far enough back to have fresh legs — could benefit from a single gap appearing at a crucial moment. This is a low-probability shape that does not depend on running style so much as race-riding fortune and cannot be planned for, but it is a genuine risk in a field of this size.

watchPoints.text: Welbury (Bethell/Orr) has won six of his last six and returns to the course and trip where he excelled — monitor his position from the 3f marker as any traffic trouble will be the main obstacle to a seventh straight win.

With five confirmed front-runners in a 20-runner field on soft ground, the opening two furlongs will be chaotic — watch for early casualties among Lion of Alba and Le Samourai if they are outpaced for the lead and drop tamely through the field.

Storming Point and Astrazar are natural prominent racers likely to be shuffled wider and further back than ideal — if either secures a better position than expected off a fast pace, reassess their winning chance immediately.

Intense Vision is flagged as a horse who fades in the finish and the stable is 0/2 in the last 14 days — monitor at the betting stage for any drift that confirms market participants share the concern about her stamina on soft ground.

Command The Stars drops sharply back in trip after running over 9f-11f and the soft ground is his best going condition — if Darragh Keenan positions him at the rear early and the race develops as a true stamina test, he is worth tracking through the final two furlongs for a late place surge.

races.name: Weatherbys Lonsdale Cup Stakes (Group 2)

runners_data.name: Caballo De Mar
runners_data.note: Suited by this trip and prominent style puts him right in the firing line tracking Amiloc; George Scott sends him here fresh after 64 days off but his record on similar going (4 wins/places from 7 sim-going runs) is encouraging, and Oisin Murphy can ensure he gets the ideal stalking position.
runners_data.comment: Beaten out of the sights last time and returning after 64 days off, Caballo De Mar is hard to fancy on these figures, though he does hold a win two starts back and has experience of today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Al Nayyir
runners_data.note: William Buick's hold-up tactics on this eight-year-old are proven over 2m+ trips, and his soft-ground record is adequate, but the slow-build tempo that Amiloc will likely set is a real threat to a horse who needs the race truly run to get competitive; his win at 14f last time out shows residual quality.
runners_data.comment: A winner four starts back and placed on two of the three runs that followed, Al Nayyir arrives with solid recent form and has run over today's trip before, but connections must be hopeful the 64-day absence has not blunted his edge under a hefty 131 lb.

runners_data.name: Amiloc
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner here, Ralph Beckett's four-year-old can dictate entirely on his own terms; recent form includes an unfinished (U) and two mid-pack finishes, but his soft-ground run (1/10 sim-going) and single prominent score suggest he can find more at the head of affairs over this staying trip.
runners_data.comment: Amiloc shaped with promise when second five starts back and arrives here on a good preparation of 24 days, but he remains winless in recent starts and the unseating last time out is a concern connections must overcome.

runners_data.name: Carmers
runners_data.note: W J Lee partners this Irish raider who has soft-ground experience (5th at Leopardstown in soft) and won over 16f, but his prominent style means he will be competing for limited real estate directly behind Amiloc; a 64-day break and Patrick Twomey's quiet 14-day record (0/12) are mild flags.

runners_data.name: Columbus
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins sends Columbus here just 20 days after his last run, and his win over 17f on good ground last year shows stamina is not in question; a hold-up horse by style, he faces the same tempo problem as Al Nayyir, and his recent form (0 on last run) is worrying heading into a competitive Group 2.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and yet to win in recent starts, Columbus showed encouragement with a third three runs back and returns here after 20 days, carrying 131 lb; lightly raced enough to suggest there is more to come.

runners_data.name: French Master
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent racer by nature — John & Thady Gosden's five-year-old has run well from the front half of the field before — but with Caballo De Mar, Carmers, and Mount Atlas all wanting similar ground, he is likely to end up racing further back than ideal; James Doyle will need to navigate traffic to get the best from him, and STYLE_FIT of 0.92 tempers expectations.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked seventh of eight on our figures, French Master makes it hard to build a case — yet he does bring distance and going experience to the table, and a second two starts back shows he can get competitive.

runners_data.name: Illinois
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore partners this Aidan O'Brien-trained five-year-old who won over 22f on good ground, confirming his stamina credentials; his natural style is prominent, but surplus pace in this field means he will likely be shuffled into mid-division against his wishes — discount his prospects unless the race develops in a way that allows him to slot closer than the pace map suggests.
runners_data.comment: Illinois shaped with promise when winning three starts back, and his official mark of 108 is undercut by a rating of 112 that suggests he retains plenty of ability over today's trip; the risk is that he has finished fifth in each of his last two starts.

runners_data.name: Mount Atlas
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's consistent performer has a fine record of placing on soft and good to soft ground (5 runs, 1 win, 4 places in sim-going), and PJ McDonald will know exactly how to slot him into a prominent position tracking Amiloc; his last win came over 14f, so the extra distance of 2m½f on soft ground is a genuine stamina query worth monitoring.
runners_data.comment: Mount Atlas arrives on the back of a win last time out and has experience of today's going, but 41 days off the track raises a fitness query and he faces seven rivals carrying 131 lb off an official mark of 112.

runners_data.name: Quickthorn
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old returning after a remarkable 707 days off the track — the absence alone is the dominant factor here; he has three wins on soft ground and ran well over 14f previously, but Hughie Morrison's 14-day record is thin (1/6) and any ring-rustiness after nearly two years away would be severely punished at Group 2 level.
runners_data.comment: Quickthorn showed he retains the ability to win when it matters, landing a victory in recent starts, and he has experience over today's trip and going to call upon; the lengthy 707-day absence is the one query, but his rating of 117 marks him as the class act in this field.

races.paceDynamic: Amiloc is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to dispute the lead, Rossa Ryan can dictate a controlled, energy-conserving gallop on good to soft ground over 2m½f — a setup that strongly favours those who can travel close to the pace rather than those forced wide or into a waiting role. The prominent cluster of Caballo De Mar, Carmers, Mount Atlas, and the redistributed Illinois and French Master creates meaningful congestion in the first three or four positions, and that bunching is likely to generate awkward shuffling two to three furlongs from home as the race ignites. The hold-up duo of Al Nayyir and Columbus will settle deepest but face the twin threats of a modest tempo and having to pick their way through a compressed midfield on a track where gaps may not appear early enough. This race shape — a single pacesetter controlling an honest but uncontested gallop — overwhelmingly suits patient, prominent-to-mid types who can track the leader through the race and mount a sustained challenge from two out rather than a sharp late burst; the field holds more prominent types than the map can place cleanly, with Caballo De Mar and Mount Atlas best positioned to actually secure their natural slots behind Amiloc, while Illinois and French Master are genuine prominent horses who will likely find themselves further back than their style demands.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Amiloc Controls, Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Amiloc dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the race unfolds as a test of stamina from two out on soft ground.
scenarios.body: Amiloc sets an honest but not brutal tempo, and those who track him in the first three or four positions get the perfect tow into the straight; soft ground ensures the finish is a sustained grind rather than a sharp sprint, rewarding those with the stamina to sustain their effort over the final half-mile.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Grinds Out Stayers
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fractionally more genuine than expected and the ground takes its toll, turning the race into a true stayers' test in the final quarter-mile.
scenarios.body: A stronger-than-usual gallop, perhaps forced by Carmers or Columbus pressing forward, stretches the field and eliminates one-paced types before the turn; horses with proven stamina and soft-ground form over extreme distances come into their own in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Carnage Favours Hold-Up
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion behind Amiloc causes interference two to three furlongs out and multiple horses check or are squeezed.
scenarios.body: Checked horses lose momentum at the critical moment, and the hold-up runners who have been waiting for a gap suddenly find daylight as the pack opens; the closers' late surge benefits from the disruption ahead, though soft ground limits how much ground can realistically be made up.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Amiloc Outstays the Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves too slow for the stalkers to quicken past and Amiloc's lead is never meaningfully threatened.
scenarios.body: A thoroughly tactical crawl followed by a moderate final-furlong sprint suits the leader who has preserved maximum energy; Amiloc, already four lengths clear entering the straight, simply extends as rivals lack the gears to close on soft ground.

watchPoints.text: Prominent congestion warning — Caballo De Mar, Carmers, Mount Atlas, Illinois, and French Master all want the same two or three berths directly behind Amiloc; watch for bumping and interference between the 7f and 3f marks as riders jostle for position.

Quickthorn's 707-day absence is unprecedented in this field — watch for any signs of ring rust in the early stages, as a horse returning after nearly two years off at Group 2 level over 2m½f on soft could be unpredictable in traffic.

Columbus's hold-up position for Mullins is risky if Amiloc sets only a crawl — watch whether Colin Keane elects to push him closer than usual to compensate, as a tactical change could disrupt the intended race shape significantly.

Track going confirmed as Good to Soft for this race despite the headline Soft designation — watch whether the firmer end of the going description benefits speed-stamina types over pure stayers, potentially compressing finishing times and reducing the premium on extreme hold-up running.

races.name: Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Gimcrack Stakes (Group 2)

runners_data.name: Adaay of Scarlett
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's front-runner has burned plenty of energy making the running in six consecutive attempts, and with four rivals equally keen to lead, Oisin Murphy faces a genuine battle to hold the rail from the off; five consecutive second-place finishes on good ground raise the question of whether she has the finishing kick to hold on if she does get clear on softer terrain.
runners_data.comment: Consistent and in excellent heart, Adaay of Scarlett has finished second in each of his last four starts and boasts experience over today's trip, with his 109 rating making him the one to beat from stall three off 128 lb.

runners_data.name: Agamemnon
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes's colt has already won on soft going and posted his best effort at 6f, making him a natural fit for today's conditions; Kieran Shoemark can afford to be patient from a prominent position knowing the pace will be fierce, and a form line that includes a soft-ground success puts him ahead of most rivals on going preference.
runners_data.comment: Second last time out and a winner four starts back, Agamemnon arrives in decent nick after 19 days and has run over today's trip, though that eighth three starts back tempers enthusiasm; the 128 lb burden and our rating of 102 suggest he sits squarely in the middle of this field.

runners_data.name: Arapaho Gold
runners_data.note: Michael Dods sends out an unbeaten three-from-three horse whose consistency over 5f and 6f on good ground is outstanding, though today's soft is an untested variable for Connor Beasley to manage; if the going doesn't blunt his electric turn of foot, he is the most dangerous stalker in the race.
runners_data.comment: Arapaho Gold arrives on the back of three consecutive victories and brings strong recent form into this contest; he has run over today's trip before and his 106 rating underlines his claims, though 128 lb is the one burden he must overcome.

runners_data.name: Final Objective
runners_data.note: James Doyle partners a horse who won last time out over course and distance on good ground, but a 7-day turnaround in Group 2 company on softer ground asks significant questions; the L-style profile means he'll be embroiled in the early battle rather than cruising into it, which is the last thing a horse needs on this ground.
runners_data.comment: Final Objective won last time out and has run over today's trip, but he carries 128 lb on a quick turnaround of just seven days, and our rating of 95 leaves him eighth of eleven in the rankings — promise and pressure in equal measure.

runners_data.name: Great Oak
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's yard is firing on all cylinders (8 winners from 32 runners in the last 14 days) and this colt destroyed a field on debut at this track, earning an eye-catching OR=120; lightly raced and genuinely unexposed, Clifford Lee can plot a course behind the pace battle and let this horse's raw ability take over, but the single run makes him a speculative commodity at Group 2 level.
runners_data.comment: Great Oak won last time out but ranks last of eleven on our figures, with a speed rating of just 44 doing little to inspire confidence; he has run over today's trip and returns after 32 days, yet it is hard to look past the gulf in class the bare numbers suggest.

runners_data.name: Hell Of A Spin
runners_data.note: Adrian Keatley's Irish raider is another natural front-runner, having led in both of his wins, and M.P. Sheehy will be scrapping for position from the gate against several rivals with the same agenda; stepping up from 5f to 6f for the first time on soft ground while fighting for the lead is a tough ask.
runners_data.comment: Hell Of A Spin was a winner two starts back and third last time out, showing consistent recent form, though ranked fifth of eleven on our rating of 104 and the step back up in weight to 128 lb from stall one may test his resolution today.

runners_data.name: Marco Polo
runners_data.note: A P O'Brien's colt ran second on debut at 6f on good ground and carries Ryan Moore — a partnership that rarely goes without a tactical plan; his true running style is forward-going rather than a genuine hold-up horse, but Moore will likely place him just off the pace to avoid the scrimmage up front, giving him the best chance to produce an unexposed engine in the straight.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in recent starts, Marco Polo faces a stiff task ranked tenth of eleven on our figures, though he has run over today's trip before and returns on a handy 12-day turnaround with a runner-up last time to his name.

runners_data.name: Matteo
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's horse won both starts over 5f on good ground but hasn't raced for 83 days, and stepping up in distance, class and ground simultaneously on a return from a lengthy absence makes this a very ambitious assignment; Kevin Stott will try to slot in behind the leaders, but the combination of unknowns is daunting.
runners_data.comment: Matteo arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and a rating of 106 underlines his claims as a serious threat, with experience over today's trip adding further confidence; the main risk is a return from 83 days off.

runners_data.name: Mrair
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand rides a horse that has won over course and distance (6f, good ground) and whose two-month break should have left him fresh; a prominent style that just trails the pace rather than making it means he is well positioned to benefit from the expected carnage up front, and George Scott's recent form (3/16 in 14 days) is solid.

runners_data.name: Mussab
runners_data.note: Richard and Peter Fahey's unexposed runner has finished third twice, over 5f and 6f respectively on good ground, so the soft and the step to Group 2 company on 62 days off are all unknowns; Colin Keane's tactical intelligence is an asset, but without a clear running style this horse is hard to map with confidence.
runners_data.comment: Twice third in recent starts, Mussab arrives here with experience over today's trip and our rating of 106 suggesting he holds strong claims as the second-ranked runner in the field, though a return of 62 days off and yet to win in his last two starts are the notes of caution.

runners_data.name: Never Enough
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's progressive filly won on her second start over 6f on good ground and William Buick takes the ride, which is a significant booking in terms of optimism from the yard; however, a front-running profile puts her right in the firing line of the pace duel, and soft ground is untested territory after both starts on good.
runners_data.comment: Ranked ninth of eleven on our figures, Never Enough is hard to fancy at this level despite winning last time out and finishing second the start before that; he has run over today's trip and returns after 27 days, but the speed rating of 71 tells its own story.

runners_data.name: Ronson
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa rides the only true hold-up horse in the race, a horse with a 5f win on good ground who steps up in distance and class after 49 days off; Ronson will be last away from the gate into a fierce pace, and if the front-runners do collapse, he gives De Sousa a live late chance, though the OR=92 makes him the longshot of the hold-up brigade.
runners_data.comment: Ran to win three starts back and was second two starts back, but fourth last time out after a 49-day absence clouds his current fitness; has run over today's trip and carries 128 lb from stall 11.

races.paceDynamic: Five front-runners — Adaay of Scarlett, Hell Of A Spin, Final Objective, Matteo, and Never Enough — will create an intense early battle for position on this flat York 6f, and with soft ground adding stamina demands, the pace is almost certain to be fierce from the outset. The leaders will burn each other up through the first three furlongs, leaving those racing prominently or just off the pace — Agamemnon, Arapaho Gold, Mrair — ideally placed to pick up the pieces as the front rank ties up in the closing stages. Great Oak and Marco Polo are lightly raced unknowns whose true tactical preference is unclear, but neither is a proven front-runner, giving them the option to stalk the pace rather than fight for it. This race shape strongly favours hold-up or prominently-raced horses with proven stamina and soft-ground ability, as the contested pace on testing ground will make it very difficult for any of the five pace-setters to last home; the field holds more front-running types than can realistically secure a clean lead, with Adaay of Scarlett and Hell Of A Spin most likely to actually dictate, meaning several others must drop back and race against their instincts.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Win
scenarios.trigger: If the five front-runners burn each other out through the first half and the soft ground stretches the field, leaving fresh legs to finish.
scenarios.body: The fierce early pace on soft turf will sap the leaders' reserves by the two-furlong pole, opening the race wide for horses that have been travelling well within themselves; Agamemnon, who has already won on soft and finished second at this track, and Mrair, a course-and-distance winner, are ideally profiled to swoop late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Rail Stalker Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent types — particularly Arapaho Gold — sits just behind the leaders and times a sustained run from two furlongs out perfectly.
scenarios.body: Arapaho Gold's unbeaten record over 6f on good ground is compelling, and stalking a strong pace before hitting the front early in the straight suits a horse that has always won with a bit in hand; the soft going is the only concern but connections are clearly confident stepping into Group 2 company.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Lightly Raced Star Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If Great Oak or Marco Polo — both OR=120 and lightly raced — translate their dominant debut performances into this stiffer Group 2 test.
scenarios.body: Great Oak won impressively at this course on good ground and K.R. Burke's yard is in superb form (T14: 8/32), and if the class ceiling of these two unexposed types is as high as their ratings suggest, they can track the pace and power through the soft without having been involved in the early battle; Marco Polo with Ryan Moore gives him every tactical chance to find cover and finish powerfully.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Adaay of Scarlett or Hell Of A Spin gets a clean break and dictates a truly measured tempo despite the apparent pace pressure, front-running rivals failing to press hard enough.
scenarios.body: This outcome requires rivals to show more restraint than their form profiles suggest, but if Adaay of Scarlett (Oisin Murphy in the saddle) replicates the tactical nous that landed her earlier wins and the other leaders don't fire out, she could control enough to hold on; this is the least likely shape given the number of horses bred to go forward.

watchPoints.text: With five horses (Adaay of Scarlett, Hell Of A Spin, Final Objective, Matteo, Never Enough) all wanting to lead over 6f on soft ground, watch for a chaotic first furlong where bumping and jostling could unbalance any of them and cause a serious pace meltdown by the halfway mark.

Arapaho Gold's unbeaten record has been built entirely on good ground — if the soft surface blunts his quick acceleration through the final two furlongs, the entire prominent-horse scenario collapses and the race falls to a hold-up type like Ronson or Agamemnon.

Great Oak and Marco Polo (both OR=120) are lightly raced and their true ability levels remain genuinely unknown — either could dramatically upgrade the race if their debut form translates, or they could be overrated on limited evidence, making them key swing factors in the outcome.

Matteo's 83-day absence combined with a simultaneous step up in trip, class and going makes him a horse to monitor in the preliminary parade — any signs of sweatiness or agitation after the long break could signal he is not fully ready, and Kevin Stott will have little margin for error from the front.

Ryan Moore's tactical choice on Marco Polo will be telling at the start — if Moore hangs back conspicuously from the gate rather than going forward, it is a strong signal that he is treating this horse as a hold-up type and has spotted the pace scenario playing into his hands.

races.name: Coolmore City Of Troy Nunthorpe Stakes (Group 1)

runners_data.name: Ain't Nobody
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist for Kevin Ryan who needs a strong pace to close into; 66 days off the track is a query, and her similar-going record shows only one placing from three starts — she needs chaos at the front.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning after 66 days off, Ain't Nobody has experience of today's distance and going but his recent form makes for grim reading; stall six and 141 lb are the neutral backdrop to what must be a sharper effort.

runners_data.name: American Affair
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's six-year-old is the form horse in the field having won his most recent start and finished second twice in five soft-ground runs from 15; Paul Mulrennan gets a handy draw type who travels prominently and handles this going well.|
runners_data.comment: American Affair won last time out and has experience of today's trip and going, but his patchy recent record — unplaced twice in his last five starts — and a rating four pounds below official suggest he faces a stiff task from stall four carrying 141 lb.

runners_data.name: Cover Up
runners_data.note: William Buick and the Crisfords have him in top form with a recent win; naturally prominent, he handles good ground best but has placed on cut and will sit just off the pace in the ideal stalking position if the front two fight.|
runners_data.comment: Cover Up won last time out and has experience of today's distance and going, but a 34-day absence and a stiff 141 lb to carry from stall 15 are both factors to weigh against him, leaving him a competitive if not straightforward proposition here.

runners_data.name: Jm Jungle
runners_data.note: John and Sean Quinn's six-year-old is a genuine prominent racer who has been placed behind faster-away types in this draw but shows consistent 5f form; with the field overloaded at the front, he may find himself a length or two off where he wants to be.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Jm Jungle does at least bring distance and going experience to the table and a third two starts back hints at residual ability, though he carries 141 lb from stall 16 and ranks 12th of 18 on our assessment.

runners_data.name: Night Raider
runners_data.note: K. R. Burke's five-year-old is one of only two confirmed front-runners and has winning form on both soft and good ground over 5f; if he outbreaks Fitzella he is the one controlling the tempo, which is a potent position.|
runners_data.comment: Night Raider brings winning form into this, scoring in two of his last five starts, and has experience of today's trip and conditions; at 141 lb from stall 2, the weight burden may be the key question mark.

runners_data.name: Partisan Hero
runners_data.note: David Loughnane's six-year-old is a genuine forward-going sort with several soft-ground placings and a 5f win on good; pressed into a midfield slot by field congestion, his chance is tempered by the likelihood he won't get his preferred position cleanly.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked 14 of 18 on our figures, Partisan Hero makes little appeal off 141 lb from stall 17, and a seventh last time out does nothing to reverse that view, though he has placed twice in recent starts and has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Redorange
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's four-year-old has two 5f wins on good ground and has been running well; PJ McDonald rides and he has a tongue tie suggesting wind surgery — form tails off on easier ground and the soft conditions are a mild concern.|
runners_data.comment: Redorange has won twice in his last five starts, including a win last time out, but our figures rank him thirteenth of eighteen in this field, and 141 lb from stall 18 makes him hard to fancy at this level despite his recent winning form over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Rumstar
runners_data.note: Jonathan Portman's six-year-old arrives in good form with a win and a second in his last two, both on good ground; Rob Hornby can hold him up just off the pace in a natural prominent position and his consistent recent form makes him a serious player.|
runners_data.comment: Rumstar arrives here in good heart following a win two starts back and a runner-up effort last time out, and he has experience of both today's trip and conditions. The chief concern is that his 141 lb burden may test him against lighter-weighted rivals.

runners_data.name: Starlust
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's five-year-old has winning form at 5f and has placed on good ground multiple times; as a natural prominent type redistributed back by field size, Rossa Ryan will need to work to find a berth, and that energy expenditure early on soft is not ideal.|
runners_data.comment: Starlust has run over today's trip and going, carries 141 lb from draw 10, and our rating of 115 marks him out as a live threat in a wide-open field — the risk is that he has been winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Bacio
runners_data.note: Wesley Ward's three-year-old arrives unbeaten in Britain and Ireland at 5f, with a 5f win on good and a second on firm, and Juan Hernandez takes the ride; 63 days off, limited soft-ground exposure, but raw ability could overcome the going question.|
runners_data.comment: Bacio arrives on the back of three successive wins and four victories in his last five starts, making him impossible to ignore at the top of the weights on 139 lb; he has run over today's trip before, and a 63-day break is the only question mark against an irresistible recent record.

runners_data.name: Mission Central
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes the mount on Aidan O'Brien's three-year-old who has won three consecutive 5f starts including a Group race; a genuine hold-up horse who needs the front runners to collapse — Moore is the ideal jockey to bide his time and produce a late challenge.|
runners_data.comment: Mission Central has won three of his last five starts, including back-to-back victories, but was well held on his most recent outing 41 days ago; he has run over today's trip before and carries 139 lb from stall seven.

runners_data.name: Asfoora
runners_data.note: Henry Dwyer's eight-year-old Australian mare has been racing in Britain and has a tongue tie and blinkers; her form on soft is limited and she has finished no better than fourth in her last five, making the conditions a concern for a mare who prefers firmer.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Asfoora at least returns on a workable 21-day break having run over today's trip and going before, though carrying 138 lb from stall 3 and ranked tenth of eighteen on ratings, she faces a stiff task off the pace.

runners_data.name: Azure Angel
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's six-year-old has a winless recent run of form and Daniel Tudhope partners her in blinkers and tongue tie; a hold-up type who ran well over course and distance when conditions suited but her 615050 recent form string is not encouraging.|
runners_data.comment: Azure Angel has been out of the placings in five of her last six starts, including an unplaced effort last time, and our figures rank her near the foot of the field; she has run over today's trip and returns on a reasonable 21-day break, but it is hard to make a case at these weights.

runners_data.name: Heavenly Heather
runners_data.note: Tracy Waggott's five-year-old has only one placing from 15 similar-going runs with no wins in that sample; a prominent-going type who will find the field's congestion particularly difficult, and her form record on cut ground makes her a tough each-way case.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Heavenly Heather arrives 41 days between runs, winless in her last six starts, and unplaced on her most recent outing, with a second three starts back the brightest recent spark; experience over today's trip and a fourth-placed finish four starts back offer slim comfort at best.

runners_data.name: Rayevka
runners_data.note: F-H Graffard's French-trained four-year-old has an excellent soft-ground record showing three wins from seven runs on similar going, and won most recently over 5f on soft; Barzalona rides and this runner's going profile is the strongest in the field — the 66-day gap is the only query.|
runners_data.comment: Rayevka won two starts back but was only second last time out, and a 66-day absence adds a fitness query; she has run over today's trip and carries 138 lb from stall 12, with our rating of 113 suggesting she holds solid claims if straight forward.

runners_data.name: Time For Sandals
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace's four-year-old has been in fair form but the 58003 recent string and no wins on soft from two tries suggests the conditions and pace shape may not play to his strengths; naturally prominent but likely to find himself a few lengths off the pace with the field overloaded.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Time For Sandals at least shaped with encouragement when third last time out, and she has run over today's distance and going before; the 138 lb burden from stall 13 may not help her cause among a field of 18.

runners_data.name: Fitzella
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's three-year-old is the second confirmed front-runner, but her form reads as a horse who has hit the front and been passed — a 56505 recent string and Colin Keane aboard; she will ensure Night Raider is tested early but may be the one to run herself into the ground.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 15 of 18 on our figures, Fitzella makes little appeal despite drawing stall 1 and returning on a fresh 19 days; she has run over today's trip before, but her recent string of fifths and worse offers scant encouragement.

runners_data.name: Pershaada
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's two-year-old is the youngest in the field and carries the lightest weight; a prominent-going type who has won twice at 5f on good ground, but the combination of her age, soft ground and being shuffled back by field congestion makes this a very tough assignment.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked well below the top-rated runners on our figures, Pershaada is hard to fancy from stall 11, though a win last time out and a second win three starts back show she knows how to find the line, and she has experience over today's trip.

races.paceDynamic: Night Raider and Fitzella are the two confirmed front-runners in an 18-runner field, and with Good To Soft ground at York's 5f, they will contest the lead from the stalls and set an honest, pressured gallop that is unlikely to be allowed to settle into anything truly even. The pack of genuinely prominent types — Cover Up, American Affair, Rumstar, Redorange, Rayevka, Bacio — will sit immediately behind on their heels, creating a dense, compressed early order that stretches the field and puts a significant premium on tactical agility. The field holds considerably more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural position; of those redistributed to the map's midfield, Partisan Hero, Jm Jungle and Time For Sandals are the most likely to press for a forward berth, while Starlust, Heavenly Heather and Pershaada will find themselves shuffled back further than their handlers would prefer. A pressured early pace on soft ground over a flat 5f overwhelmingly favours horses who can race prominently without hitting the front too soon — the "racing into it" prominent type who settles just off the speed will be ideally placed when the front two tie each other up in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Duel, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Night Raider and Fitzella fight hard for the lead and drain each other's reserves in the soft ground, handing the race to a prominent tracker who swoops late off their shoulders.
scenarios.body: The contested early fractions on Good To Soft take their toll on both front-runners inside the final furlong, leaving a runner who has settled just off the boil in pole position to pick up the pieces; the soft ground amplifies this effect as early expenditure proves punishing.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Night Raider Controls, Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Night Raider is allowed to set a measured, uncontested pace and his rival Fitzella fails to match him from the off, enabling a controlled front-running display.
scenarios.body: Night Raider has winning form on soft and good-to-soft and is trained by K. R. Burke in hot form; a lone lead at a fair clip suits his galloping style and gives him first run on the field approaching the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Storm Through
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely fierce and the front-runners collapse in the last 100 yards, allowing hold-up horses to finish powerfully through a tiring field.
scenarios.body: Mission Central and Ain't Nobody, both genuine hold-up types with Ryan Moore and Kevin Stott respectively, are the only runners truly suited to a late swoop; Mission Central's three consecutive wins including a Group race mark him as the classiest closer in the field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Type Finds Gap
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace bunches the field and one of the prominent horses forced wide or back finds a clear run through the middle to benefit from a clear passage.
scenarios.body: A horse like Jm Jungle or Partisan Hero, pushed out of their natural position at the start, occasionally finds compensation if the field fans wide in the straight and creates a gap; soft ground can produce unexpected separations across the track.

watchPoints.text: Rayevka's soft-ground record — three wins from seven similar-going runs — is the single most relevant form factor in the race; if she handles the step up to Group 1 company, the going is entirely in her favour.

Mission Central and Ryan Moore represent the biggest hold-up threat — if Night Raider and Fitzella genuinely set a strong pace and tie each other up, Moore will have Mission Central poised to pounce inside the final furlong.

Night Raider and Fitzella are on a direct collision course for the early lead; watch which one establishes control in the first two furlongs, as the one who has to fight will have spent vital reserves on the soft ground.

Bacio's unbeaten British form and Wesley Ward's record with sprinters makes him dangerous on form, but 63 days off the track and limited soft-ground exposure are two flags to monitor — watch how he handles the going in the first furlong.

The redistribution of Partisan Hero, Jm Jungle, Time For Sandals, Starlust, Heavenly Heather and Pershaada from prominent positions creates a genuinely compressed mid-pack; watch the draw and early running positions at the start to see which of them finds their spot and which gets buried.

races.name: Assured Data Protection Handicap Stakes (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Plage De Havre
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Andrew Balding who has won at 1m4f on good ground (1/12f/GOO) and finished third at the same trip; solid going handler but recent form is patchy (639), and at 48 days since last run may need to sharpen up in a competitive handicap.
runners_data.comment: Plage De Havre shaped with clear promise when third two starts back, and a winner four starts back, carrying 138 lb off a top-rated profile that marks him as a leading contender; the chief concern is that ninth last time out leaves his current form under a cloud.

runners_data.name: Wave Rider
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes over on this George Scott-trained four-year-old who has a win and four placed efforts at 1m2f on good; the step up to 1m4f on softer ground is the key query, but sim-going figures (4/13, 1W4P) suggest he handles cut, and the top jockey booking is significant.
runners_data.comment: Wave Rider showed a win and a second in recent starts but has been unplaced twice since, and at 137 lb he faces a stiff weight task; experience on today's going is a plus, and 24 days off suggests he returns fresh.

runners_data.name: French Duke
runners_data.note: James Doyle rides for Hamad Al Jehani and this five-year-old has a 1m4f win on good to his name, though six of his last six have yielded only one placed finish on similar ground; at only 1/3 trainer 14-day strike rate, the yard is not in a hot vein.
runners_data.comment: French Duke won five starts back and returns here fit on a 15-day turnaround, with experience of today's trip and going in his favour; carrying 135 lb is worth noting, but his overall profile makes him our pick at a rating of 104.

runners_data.name: Master Vintner
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's four-year-old arrives in excellent form with three consecutive placed efforts including a win at 1m2f on good; the headgear (blinkers) is retained and Rossa Ryan partners — handles cut and should stay 1m4f, but finding the front-running berth may cost energy here.
runners_data.comment: Master Vintner won last time out and has placed in two of his three starts before that, so current form is solid, though his speed rating of 84 and rank of ninth of sixteen suggest he faces a stiff ask at 134 lb.

runners_data.name: Ernst Blofeld
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope rides this genuine hold-up performer for the Al Jehani yard; his one win came at 1m2f on standard, and there is a stamina question over 1m4f, but his off-the-pace style means he will dodge the early prominent scramble entirely — the race shape suits his profile directly.
runners_data.comment: Won three starts back but has offered little since, finishing seventh and then fifth in his most recent outings, and at 133 lb off a mark of 95 he faces a stiff ask; has run over today's trip and retains some ability, but needs to recapture that earlier form after 41 days off.

runners_data.name: Tycoon
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore rides for Kevin Philippart De Foy and this four-year-old has a 1m2f win on good plus multiple placed efforts; soft ground was a concern (13th at 1m2f/Soft) but Moore's positional intelligence should help him secure a clean prominent berth if it exists.
runners_data.comment: Tycoon has been knocking at the door, finishing third two starts back and runner-up last time out 27 days ago, and he has experience of today's distance and going; carrying 132 lb while yet to win in recent starts is the main concern.

runners_data.name: Master Builder
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand partners this David Menuisier five-year-old returning from 100 days off; his 1m2f win on good is the headline form but he has previous stamina-sapping runs at 1m4f on soft (7th and 3rd), so the fitness query is real after that layoff.
runners_data.comment: Bounced back to win last time out, which is the obvious positive, but two unplaced efforts before that and a 100-day absence since give reason for caution; he has run over today's trip and going, and 130 lb is no featherweight ask on a comeback.

runners_data.name: Sportingsilvermine
runners_data.note: Marco Ghiani rides this consistent James Owen five-year-old who has two wins from 15 attempts at 1m2f; his soft-ground sim stats are modest (0W2P from 4) and the step up to 1m4f is unproven — he may find this distance on this ground beyond his optimum.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well adrift of the field on our figures, Sportingsilvermine is hard to fancy despite two wins in his last six starts, though he arrives here on a snappy 13-day turnaround with experience of today's distance and going to call upon.

runners_data.name: Say What You See
runners_data.note: Billy Garritty's mount is a natural prominent type by instinct, having won at 1m2f and 1m4f on good and standard; the crowded prominent group means he is unlikely to secure his preferred position without burning significant early energy, which tempers confidence in his ability to reproduce his best.
runners_data.comment: Ranked a lowly 13th of 16 on our figures, Say What You See is hard to fancy at the weights despite a lively recent sequence that includes a winner two starts back and a runner-up last time out; he has the experience of today's trip and going, but the speed rating of 86 makes him a tough sell.

runners_data.name: Truth Be Told
runners_data.note: W J Lee partners this progressive four-year-old trained in Ireland who has won twice recently at 1m2f and 1m4f on good; his front-running tendencies are well documented, but with Explode and a host of others ahead of him in the race map, his chance is conditioned on whether he can work onto the pace without overexerting.

runners_data.name: Explode
runners_data.note: William Buick rides for Faye Bramley and this is the one confirmed front-runner in the field — two recent wins at 1m2f on good and a second in a 2m contest suggest he stays well; only 6 days since last run is worth monitoring, but Buick will dictate terms and his ability to control the fractions is the central tactical pivot of this race.
runners_data.comment: Explode arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and clearly in the form of his life, with experience over today's trip and going working in his favour; however, a return in just six days and a patchy record before that purple patch — including an eighth and two other poor efforts in his last five — give reason for caution at 128 lb.

runners_data.name: Zanndabad
runners_data.note: Jamie Spencer pilots this seven-year-old for A.J. Martin, a genuine hold-up type proven over extreme distances (wins at 1m10f and 1m6f on soft) — the drop to 1m4f is almost certainly short of his optimum, but soft ground and Spencer's patient style means he will be finishing on strongly in the closing stages if the pace is genuine.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and beaten a long way back in three of them, Zanndabad at least has experience over today's trip and a speed rating that hints at more ability than his recent efforts suggest, though 55 days off and 127 lb are questions he must answer.

runners_data.name: Shadow Dance
runners_data.note: Rebecca Menzies's six-year-old has headgear (tongue strap and cheekpieces) and a 139-day absence — a combination that demands caution; her natural style leans prominent but with a weak soft-ground record (0W4P in 15 similar-ground runs) and the long layoff, she faces a stiff task even in the right shape.
runners_data.comment: Shadow Dance arrives here 139 days fresh, and a rating of 104 puts him notably ahead of his official mark of 89, suggesting he holds strong claims — yet his recent string of unplaced and mid-field efforts makes it hard to trust he can finally get his head in front.

runners_data.name: Genealogy
runners_data.note: Clifford Lee rides stablemate to Explode for Faye Bramley — a hold-up type who has won at 1m4f on good (twice in his last three runs) and has form at further; soft ground is untested and at 40 days since last run he arrives fresh, but his position profile means he avoids the prominent traffic chaos completely.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked 11 of 16 here, Genealogy at least has experience over today's trip and going to call on, and 40 days off may have freshened him; the 126 lb burden is the obvious concern against stronger rivals.

runners_data.name: Primo Lara
runners_data.note: Colin Keane partners this Jane Chapple-Hyam five-year-old who has back-to-back wins and arrives in very good nick; his victories came at 1m2f on good and standard, so the combination of 1m4f and soft ground is the question — Keane will ride a patient race from off the pace, which suits the race dynamics here.
runners_data.comment: Ranked near the foot of this field on our figures, Primo Lara faces a stiff task, yet back-to-back wins in his last two starts give him genuine momentum, and he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Jimmy Speaking
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa takes the ride on this five-year-old who has won twice at shorter trips on good and standard; his natural inclination is to race prominently but the sheer volume of horses wanting that role means he will have to settle further back than ideal — a style mismatch that reduces his winning prospects at this trip and on this ground.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well down the field on our figures and winless in his last four starts, Jimmy Speaking faces a stiff ask here, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a handy 15-day turnaround carrying 122 lb.

runners_data.name: Cuff It
runners_data.note: Saffie Osborne rides this lightly-raced three-year-old for Richard Spencer, who is making just her third career start; soft ground produced a win at 1m2f and the step to 1m4f is plausible on pedigree, but the age and experience disadvantage against handicap-hardened older horses, combined with her natural prominent style being squeezed back by the field dynamics, make this a tough ask.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and rated 5 lb below his official mark, Cuff It faces a stiff task, though he does arrive on the back of a win two starts ago and has experience of today's going.

races.paceDynamic: Explode is the sole confirmed front-runner and, ridden by William Buick, is likely to stride into a clear lead from the outset and control a measured gallop on Good to Soft ground over 1m4f — a trip and surface he has won on in recent form. Behind him, a congested prominent group featuring Plage De Havre, Wave Rider, French Duke, Master Vintner, Tycoon, Master Builder and Sportingsilvermine will jostle for position in the early exchanges, creating genuine traffic risk between 2f and 3f out as riders compete for the best berths. This field contains more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate: Say What You See, Truth Be Told, Shadow Dance, Jimmy Speaking and Cuff It are all natural prominent racers who will be pushed into a midfield role against their instincts. The race shape strongly favours genuine hold-up horses — Ernst Blofeld, Zanndabad, Primo Lara and Genealogy — who can bypass the prominent-group scramble and pick off tiring rivals in the straight on soft ground that will increasingly test stamina.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Explode Controls, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Explode sets a comfortable lead and the prominent congestion causes traffic problems 3f out, allowing hold-up horses to sweep through.
scenarios.body: Explode's controlled front-running sets a gallop that is honest but not brutal, leaving enough in the tank for a late duel, while the hold-up brigade find clear daylight on the outside in the final 2f as the prominent group's efforts come to nothing in the soft ground. Ernst Blofeld and Primo Lara, both genuine off-the-pace types, are ideally suited to this shape — one clean run and they can pick off rivals who have wasted energy in the prominent scrimmage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Survivor Grinds It Out
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group settles quickly behind Explode and one runner secures a clean, uncontested stalking berth to challenge turning in.
scenarios.body: A horse that slots in second or third without burning energy in the early scramble is perfectly placed to take over from Explode between 2f and 1f out, relying on stamina rather than a turn of foot. Wave Rider, Master Vintner and Tycoon all have the class and jockey quality to secure that position and grind out a victory in testing conditions.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Deep Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion produces a contested, faster-than-expected early pace that burns out the stalkers, triggering a stamina-based finish.
scenarios.body: Soft ground drains the field and only those held up furthest off the pace in the first mile arrive at the 2f pole with reserves intact, enabling a sweeping late move. Zanndabad, a proven soft-ground stayer who has won at 1m6f and beyond on similar going, and Genealogy, who has form at 2m on good ground, each have the stamina profile to thrive when rivals have nothing left to give.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Prominent Lands
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is so orderly that several jockeys aggressively push their redistributed horses forward into their natural prominent position early, reducing midfield congestion.
scenarios.body: Truth Be Told or Say What You See, both genuinely effective when allowed to race prominently, could work their way into contention if the pace is unexpectedly sedate and the prominent group thins out. However, both are racing out of their natural role given the field composition, and the likelihood of all the displaced prominent types successfully reclaiming their position simultaneously is low.

watchPoints.text: Explode (Buick) will dictate every fraction — if he steals an uncontested lead of 3+ lengths by the 1m mark, the hold-up horses will need an exceptional turn of foot to reel him in on soft ground.

Prominent congestion between 2f and 3f out — with seven horses all wanting positions 2nd through 5th, Ernst Blofeld, Primo Lara and Zanndabad must find a clean passage on the outer or risk being blocked when the race ignites.

Truth Be Told and Say What You See will likely fight for position in the first 2f; watch whether either rider chooses to drop in and settle rather than burn energy — if they do, the race shape shifts meaningfully.

Master Builder returns from 100 days off — watch his early movement out of the stalls and whether Marquand settles him quickly; a fresh horse in a prominent group scramble can cause interference at a crucial point.

Zanndabad's historical trip is significantly further than 1m4f — watch his finishing position relative to the field's closing stages to assess whether Spencer has ridden him as a pacemaker sighter or a genuine contender.
